title: How to read this
intro: Moroccans text in Latin letters, borrowing a few numbers for sounds English doesn't have. This is foundational — learn these six and you can read everything else in the course. The numbers were chosen because they *look* like the Arabic letter they stand for.

symbols.sound: a throaty 'a', pushed from deep in the throat
a breathy H, like fogging up a mirror
a deep K, further back than an English k
a catch in the voice, the stop in 'uh-oh'
a soft gargle, like a French R

quiz.prompt: Which stands for a breathy H from the throat?
